questions.explanation: The only positive factor of 1 is 1. A prime must have exactly two different positive factors and be greater than 1.
Seven has exactly two positive factors: 1 and 7. Nine has 1, 3 and 9; fifteen has 1, 3, 5 and 15.

questions.prompt: Which is the only even prime number?
questions.explanation: Two has factors 1 and 2. Every even whole number greater than 2 also has 2 as an additional factor.

title: Prime numbers: why does 1 get left out?

sources.name: OpenStax — Prealgebra 2e: Find Multiples and Factors
OpenStax — Contemporary Mathematics: Prime and Composite Numbers

practice: Keep playing with numbers in a quick round of Math Rush.

sections.html:
A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 with exactly two different positive factors: 1 and itself. A factor divides a number exactly, leaving no remainder. OpenStax explains this two-factor rule.

Imagine arranging biscuits on a tray. Six biscuits can form two rows of three. Seven are less cooperative: for a complete rectangle, you can only make one row of seven or seven rows of one. Seven is prime. Nobody needs to eat the awkward biscuit.
sections.title: The number that refuses to split

sections.html:
The positive factors of 7 are 1 and 7. The factors of 9 are 1, 3 and 9: three different factors, so 9 is composite. That means a whole number greater than 1 with more than two positive factors.

OpenStax connects primes with these possible groupings. Think back to sharing equally: can you make more than one group, with more than one item in each, and nothing left over?
sections.title: Give every factor a seat

sections.html:
One has only one positive factor: 1. Saying “1 and itself” names the same factor twice. It does not create two different factors.

So 1 is neither prime nor composite. It fails the two-factor test for primes and the more-than-two test for composites. There is no missing category to memorise; count the different factors and the exception makes sense.
sections.title: Why is 1 not a prime number?

sections.html:
The first five prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11. Two has exactly the factors 1 and 2, making it the only even prime. Every larger even number also has 2 as a factor, alongside 1 and itself.

But being odd is not a membership pass: 9 and 15 are odd and composite. Here is a quick check for a positive whole number: count its different positive factors. Two? Prime. More than two? Composite. Only one? You have found 1 again, sitting happily at its own table.
sections.title: The even number allowed into the club

description: Seven biscuits, a stubborn number and a tiny counting rule. Discover what makes a prime number, why 1 is neither prime nor composite, and why 2 is special.
